Hi Sophie + Datadog partners team,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We ran a short internal exercise and think there's a narrow, high-impact research project we could run together to establish market-fit for a Redwood-hosted "observability bridge" that natively exports runtime traces/metrics to Grafana and Datadog with minimal customer config.

Proposal (high level):
- Run a 6-week research pilot with 3 early adopter customers (one Grafana-heavy, one Datadog-heavy, one mixed)
- Deliverables: connector perf profile, ops runbook, sample OTLP config, and joint customer playbook
- Success criteria: under 50ms p95 added latency; <10% config changes from customer side; 2 pilot customers sign LOI for beta

All — quick status update after a short perf run this morning. I used the sample-otlp-config.yaml and simulated a 120k spans/min workload carved to a single service. Results:
- p50 added latency: 12ms; p95: 68ms (when batch size = 256 and cache enabled)
- CPU footprint: ~6 vCPU; mem 9GB for the connector instance in our baseline; GPU not required for forwarding-only mode
- If we enable aggressive batching + KV cache reuse, p95 drops to ~44ms but increases jitter during burst windows

Questions for the pilot checklist:
1) Can Grafana accept batched OTLP payloads (yes/no + recommended max batch size)?
2) Datadog: are there ingestion best-practices for spikes and backpressure?

I can prepare a short perf appendix to the scope doc. Recommend we schedule the technical kickoff with ACME and set a 6-week timeline with weekly 30m syncs.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
